lessons.title: Two stars and one small wish
lessons.goal: I can find two useful parts and choose one small change.
success: I can use a real piece of my own work.
I can give two stars with clear reasons.
I can choose and test one small wish.
words: review
Look or listen to your work again.
star
One part of your work that helps your idea.
wish
One small change you want to make.
improve
Make one part work better for your idea.
review_steps: Use your real work. Notice a mark, gap, sound or move.
Choose one part that helps your idea. Say why.
Choose a different part that helps your idea. Say why.
Choose one small change. Try it, then say what happened.

picture_prompts.label: Look or listen
picture_prompts.prompt: Show your real work. What do you notice?
picture_prompts.description: An eye means look. You may listen or direct an adult too.

picture_prompts.label: Star 1
picture_prompts.prompt: One part helps my idea because ___.
picture_prompts.description: A star marked 1. Point to one real feature.

picture_prompts.label: Star 2
picture_prompts.prompt: Another part helps my idea because ___.
picture_prompts.description: A star marked 2. Choose a different real feature.

picture_prompts.label: Wish and change
picture_prompts.description: A small tool means make one real change, then check it.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Choose your own real work from weeks 2 to 4.
It can be paint, a print, sound or a silent piece.
You can share with just an adult.
stages.say: Find one piece you actually made, or the real note of your sound or silent sequence. Choose something from weeks two to four that you can review today. We look at choices in the work, not at how good a person is. There are no scores, rankings or competitions. A made-up feeling or abstract idea is enough. If work is missing, make a tiny honest fresh piece now and date it today before reviewing it.
stages.good: The pupil chooses actual own work or makes a small dated fresh piece. The adult identifies the true medium and makes private sharing available without asking for personal disclosure.
stages.fallback: Use a real witnessed movement note, or let the pupil direct a short silent sequence now. State honestly whether this is an earlier piece or a fresh one made today.
stages.answer: A fresh piece is a valid honest starting point. It must not be labelled as missing work from an earlier week.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Look at the eye, two stars and tool pictures.
The stars are useful parts in your work.
The wish is one small change you can make.
stages.say: Read each picture label aloud. The eye reminds us to look or listen. Star one and star two each name a different feature that helps the maker's idea. They are observations, not points or prizes. The tool reminds us to choose a wish we can act on, then check it. A star needs more than 'nice'. A wish needs more than 'make it better'.
stages.good: The pupil can identify the purpose of the picture prompts and distinguish a specific feature from a score or vague praise.
stages.fallback: Read the four labels and model them through a short silent sequence. The pupil may point to a picture, choose a spoken label or direct the adult.
stages.answer: Useful star: 'The slow ending helps my calm idea.' Useful wish: 'Add a longer pause before the end.' Vague praise or a general judgement about the pupil is not a feature-based review.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch the adult review a real class model.
Star 1 names one useful part. Star 2 names another.
The wish names one small action.
Watch a test on spare paper or in a short rehearsal.
stages.say: Use an actual adult example, not a pupil's piece. For a calm sound model, star one is the gentle volume because it suits the idea; star two is the slow ending because it feels still to me. My wish is to add a longer pause before that ending. I perform the original, then rehearse the changed pause and note what really happened. For visual art, I might value a clear curve and an open space, then test wider spacing on a spare version. I keep the original state and label the test as a test. The model is not pupil evidence.
stages.good: Two different features are linked to the maker's intention, followed by one achievable action and a real small test. Before and test states use the same art form and remain honestly identified.
stages.fallback: Actually perform a short silent curve-and-pause sequence. Name two observed features, then try a longer pause in a second performance. The pupil can direct the adult's actions and compare them.
stages.answer: Ask: 'Is my wish a small action I can do, or only a word like better?' Expected: a small action. If unclear, compare 'make it better' with 'add a pause before the end'.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Help review an adult class model.
Choose two different useful features.
Choose one wish that names a small action.
Try it on a spare test or in a rehearsal.
stages.say: Use the picture prompts in order. Ask what the maker intended, then accept two feature-based stars. Let pupils choose one small, feasible wish. Hinge: Which wish can we act on today: A 'be the best', or B 'make the pause before the ending longer'? We will test the action and record the true effect. Keep our class review separate from pupils' own evidence.
stages.good: The pupil selects B, gives or confirms two distinct observed features, and directs a real test of one achievable change. No pupil is ranked against another.
stages.fallback: Use a short adult silent sequence and the same four spoken or pictured prompts. The pupil directs one changed pause or size while keeping the rest of the sequence the same.
stages.answer: B is specific and manageable. If A is chosen, model one small action and ask a parallel check: 'Which can I do: be perfect, or move these two marks farther apart on a spare test?' Continue when the pupil identifies a real action.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your book or arts log, use one real piece.
Give star 1 and star 2. Point to each feature.
Choose one small wish and say why.
Test it on spare paper or in a short rehearsal.
Keep the before state, test and your own words.
stages.say: Start with what the piece is intended to show. Use the pictures and words to name two different helpful features, such as a clear mark and a gap, or a gentle volume and a pause. Choose one achievable wish linked to that intention. Keep the actual original state before testing. For a drawing or painting, use spare paper or a small copy for the test. For a dry fold print, do not force a change onto the original: make a small new trial on fresh paper with changed spacing, following the safe fold-print steps. For sound or movement, perform the real original sequence, then rehearse the one chosen change. Compare like forms. If the old form cannot be accessed, make a tiny fresh piece in the accessible form and review that honestly today. An adult may handle materials under the pupil's direction.
stages.good: A review of actual own work has two feature-based stars, one doable wish and a real small test. The original remains available as the before state. The test has the same form as the work being reviewed; a new form is labelled as a fresh piece, not a false before-and-after improvement.
stages.fallback: The pupil performs or directs a short silent sequence, uses two spoken or pictured stars, chooses one wish and actually rehearses that change. The adult records the real actions, pupil reasons and support when a recording method is available.
stages.answer: Example only: Star one is a clear curve because it fits calm. Star two is the gap because it gives the curve space. My wish is a wider final gap. I test it on spare paper and say what changed. The pupil may choose a different justified feature.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Tell an adult your two stars and one wish.
Show what your real test changed.
Choose the one action for next time.
Tidy and keep the original and test together.
stages.say: Listen to the maker's reasons without diagnosing their feelings. Ask what the test actually changed and whether the action is still suitable for the intended piece. A test may need another small adjustment; keep that truth visible. No improvement is invented. Use the final two minutes to put tools away, leave wet trials flat and keep each original, test and log together. Sharing with just an adult is enough.
stages.good: The pupil links the two stars and chosen wish to actual features, reports the real test result and selects a feasible next action. Work and records are safely stored.
stages.fallback: An adult witnesses the before and test silent sequences and reads a short comparison back. The pupil confirms the action to use next time or chooses a smaller one.
stages.answer: A useful review names a feature and its effect, such as a longer pause making the ending clearer to the maker. A test that did not help is recorded honestly and leads to a smaller achievable wish.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: Star 1 is ___ because ___.
Star 2 is ___ because ___.
My wish is to ___ to help ___.
My real test showed ___.
stages.say: Keep the actual date, piece or witnessed sequence, two stars, one wish and the real test result. Scribe exact words if needed, read them back and allow correction. State whether the piece came from an earlier week or was made fresh today. Retain the before state and the small test for lesson two. This is the pupil's review, not an adult score.
stages.good: A dated entry records two specific strengths, one feasible action and the observed test. It refers to real own work and preserves an honest starting point for revision.
stages.fallback: Take an oral or gestured review after the live test. The adult makes an accurate dated action note and retains the pupil's confirmed words when a recording method is available.
stages.answer: Example only: Star one is a soft start because it suits calm. Star two is a clear ending because I know when it stops. My wish is to add a longer pause before the end. My real test showed the pause was easier to notice.

Supported: Find real own work or make a tiny piece today.
Use the pictures to choose two helpful parts.
Choose one small wish with an adult.
Try the change. Keep what really happened.
Independent: Review one real piece with two stars and one wish.
Give a reason linked to each feature.
Test the one small wish in the same art form.
Keep the original, test and your review.
Aspire: Complete the two stars and one wish.
Explain how the wish builds on a useful part.
Test one small change and compare it with the start.
Choose the next action for a clear reason.

log: My real piece or sequence is ___.
Star 1 is ___ because ___.
Star 2 is ___ because ___.
My wish is to ___ to help ___.
My real test showed ___.
misconceptions: Stars are scores or a contest between pupils
Each star names a helpful feature in the maker's own work. There are no ratings, rankings or comparisons of personal worth.
A wish can just say make it better
Choose one small action linked to the intention, such as widening a gap or adding a pause. Try the action and record its real effect.
A dry fold print must be painted over to improve it
Keep the original. A new version on fresh paper can test a changed spacing. Retain both and label them as original and new trial.
Missing earlier work can be described as if it is here
Make a tiny honest fresh piece today, label the actual date and review it. Never invent work or observations from an earlier week.
kit: For four pupils: four chosen real pieces from weeks two to four, or accurate sound/movement records; four books or arts logs and four pencils. Keep original work and any chosen trial together in four labelled spaces.
Provide the four picture-and-word prompts for each pupil, or display/read them aloud. The meaning must not depend on colour alone. Adult models are separate from pupil work.

Visual tests: eight small spare sheets, familiar drawing tools and materials actually needed by the chosen piece. Paint uses a small amount of familiar washable non-toxic paint, five brushes, four mats, two stable water pots, cloths and drying space if needed.
Fold-print tests use fresh small paper, three pea-sized dabs on one half, a clear fold/edge border, gentle pressing and flat drying. Do not force wet paint or glue onto a dry original print.

Sound or silent review needs a quiet seated space, a clear stop cue and actual sequence notes if available. Keep sound below talking volume. No recording device is required; pupils may direct an adult.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show a real adult example. Say: I notice this work before I change it. My first star is one feature and why it helps.
15 to 30 seconds
Point to a second different feature. Say: My second star has its own reason. These are observations, not points or prizes.
30 to 45 seconds
Choose one small wish. Try it on spare paper or in a short silent rehearsal while keeping the original state. Say: I can actually do this action.
45 to 60 seconds
Compare the real test with the start. Say: I record what happened. I keep the original and choose one action for next time.
models: Teacher model only: Star one is a clear curve because it fits calm. Star two is an open gap because it gives the curve space. My wish is to make the final gap wider. I test that on spare paper.
Teacher model only: I review a silent sequence. Star one is a slow curve. Star two is a clear stop. My wish is a longer pause before the stop. I actually rehearse that pause and record what happened.
lessons.cover: Use one actual pupil piece or a truthful fresh small piece made today. Read the four picture-and-word prompts: look or listen, star one, star two, wish and change. Model two different feature-based stars and one small action. Let pupils test that action on spare work or in a same-form rehearsal, retaining the original before state. A dry fold print can have a new trial on fresh paper; do not force an alteration onto the original. For no materials, actually perform or direct a silent sequence and review a real changed rehearsal. Keep the actual medium, two stars, wish, test and next action in the log. Follow the seven-stage timing and final two Review minutes for tidy-up.

lessons.title: Making one real improvement
lessons.goal: I can make one real change and say how it helps my piece.
success: I can find the real work and my chosen wish.
I can make one real change in the same art form.
I can keep the before and after states and a reason.
words: review
Look or listen to your work again.
wish
One small change you want to make.
revise
Make a new or changed version.
improve
Make one part work better for your idea.
review_steps: Use your real work. Notice a mark, gap, sound or move.
Choose one part that helps your idea. Say why.
Choose a different part that helps your idea. Say why.
Choose one small change. Try it, then say what happened.

picture_prompts.label: Look or listen
picture_prompts.prompt: Show your real work. What do you notice?
picture_prompts.description: An eye means look. You may listen or direct an adult too.

picture_prompts.label: Star 1
picture_prompts.prompt: One part helps my idea because ___.
picture_prompts.description: A star marked 1. Point to one real feature.

picture_prompts.label: Star 2
picture_prompts.prompt: Another part helps my idea because ___.
picture_prompts.description: A star marked 2. Choose a different real feature.

picture_prompts.label: Wish and change
picture_prompts.description: A small tool means make one real change, then check it.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real piece, two stars and one wish.
Look at your actual test from last time.
Choose the one change you will make today.
stages.say: Use the actual piece and review from yesterday. Ask the maker to point to the two helpful features and the chosen wish. Check that the wish is one small action, not a score or vague judgement. If the work or review is missing, make a tiny fresh piece and a short honest review now, dated today. Do not invent missing earlier states. Keep a before state before changing anything.
stages.good: The pupil identifies actual own work, a feasible wish and an honest before state, or creates a dated fresh starting piece that can be revised in the same lesson.
stages.fallback: Read the witnessed silent sequence and review, or let the pupil direct a short fresh sequence now. Observe and note that starting state before the chosen change.
stages.answer: A fresh small piece and one real revision today are valid. The record must distinguish that from work recovered from an earlier week.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Which wish names an action?
Make it perfect, or add a pause before the end?
How will you know what changed?
stages.say: A useful wish tells us what to do. Compare a vague judgement with adding one pause or widening one gap. Ask how we will retain the before state and observe the after state. The two versions should use the same art form so the comparison is fair. A new art form is a fresh response, not a false revision of a different medium.
stages.good: The pupil selects a specific action and identifies a real before-and-after comparison in the same form.
stages.fallback: Perform a short silent sequence, then ask the pupil to direct one longer pause. Name the original and revised actions aloud and keep a precise witness note when recording is available.
stages.answer: Adding a pause is an action. Before and after can be two pieces, a sketch and actual changed piece, two work-only images or two precisely witnessed same-form sequences. A device is optional.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch one wish become a real change.
Keep the before state.
Make the change. Check its effect.
Say what the real after state shows.
stages.say: Show a real adult before version and state its two feature-based stars. My one wish is a longer pause before the ending of my calm silent sequence. I perform the original, then actually make the revised sequence with that pause. I compare like with like and say the pause is clearer to me. For a fold print, I keep the original dry print and make a new version on fresh paper with wider spacing, using three small dabs on one half, a clear border, gentle pressing and flat drying. I label this a revised version, not a hidden alteration of the old print. I only claim an effect that the real results show.
stages.good: The adult makes one actual chosen revision and retains both real states or precise observations. The reason links a feature to the intention, with no automatic claim that every change is better.
stages.fallback: Actually perform or direct the original silent sequence and the revised sequence. Keep all actions the same except the one chosen pause, size or spacing. The pupil can direct the adult without moving.
stages.answer: Ask: 'Did I only write my wish, or did I make the changed sequence?' Expected: made the changed sequence. If unclear, show the before and after pause lengths again and name the observed difference.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Help make one chosen class change.
Keep the real before and after states.
Say which feature changed and why.
The model is not your own evidence.
stages.say: Use an actual adult visual or silent example. Pupils direct one changed feature, then compare the observed states. Hinge: Which shows a revision happened: A only a sentence saying 'I will change it', or B the real changed work or a witnessed changed sequence? We name what actually happened and its effect for the maker's idea.
stages.good: The pupil chooses B and identifies a real changed feature. The class comparison uses the same form, and the adult model remains separate from pupil evidence.
stages.fallback: Witness an original and revised silent action sequence directed by the pupil. Use the pictured or spoken tool prompt to ask what changed and how it helps the intended idea.
stages.answer: B shows a change was made. If A is chosen, contrast the planned action with the performed one. Parallel check: 'If I wrote wider gap but the gap stayed the same, have I made that change?' Expected: no. Continue when the pupil can identify one real revised feature.

stages.name: Create
pupil: In your book or arts log, keep the real before state.
Use your one wish to make a small change.
For a dry print, you may make a new revised print.
Compare the same kind of work before and after.
Keep the real result and your own reason.
stages.say: Choose a manageable revision linked to the wish. For a painting or drawing, first keep a small sketch, work-only image or other accurate record of the before state, then make the one safe chosen change. For a dry fold print, keep the first print intact and make a new version on fresh paper with the chosen spacing or colour change. Use three pea-sized dabs on one half, a clear fold-and-edge border, gentle pressing and flat drying. Never force paint, glue or rubbing onto a dry original. For sound or silent movement, perform or direct the actual before sequence, then make the same sequence with the one intended change. Compare like forms. If the original medium is inaccessible, make a tiny fresh baseline in the accessible medium, date it today and actually revise that. Review the real effect; if a test did not help, select a smaller feasible action and carry it out rather than inventing improvement. Keep sound below talking volume and use the stop cue. Adult handling follows the pupil's direction.
stages.good: One real intentional change is made to actual own work or a clearly labelled same-form revised version. Before and after states or precise witness records exist, with a pupil-owned reason. The record says what changed and whether it helped the intended effect, without inventing success or hiding an unchanged result.
stages.fallback: The pupil performs or verbally directs a short silent baseline and a revised sequence with one real changed pause, pace, size or order. The adult witnesses both and records the actual difference, intended effect, pupil reason and support when a recording method is available.
stages.answer: Example only: I kept my first silent sequence. I made the pause longer in the revised one. I can show the difference, and the longer pause helps my calm idea. A physical fold-print revision keeps both actual prints. A changed medium is labelled as fresh work before revising it.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show the real before and after states.
Say: I changed ___ to help ___.
Point to what actually changed.
Tidy and keep both states with your log.
stages.say: Ask the maker to identify the actual changed feature and the intended effect. The maker may say more practice is needed; retain that truth. If there is no real change yet, help choose one small accessible action and actually try it now. Do not replace evidence with praise or a planned sentence. Keep private sharing available. Use the final two minutes to put tools away, leave wet work flat and retain both states or precise same-form witness records with the log.
stages.good: The pupil demonstrates or confirms one actual revised feature, explains a reason and reviews its real effect. Before and after evidence is retained, and no pupil is ranked or pressured to disclose a private story.
stages.fallback: An adult witnesses a repeat of the original and revised silent sequence if needed, reads the difference back and lets the pupil correct the record.
stages.answer: A useful review says what changed and why it may help the intended idea. It can honestly note that further practice is needed. The work, not a general adult judgement, supports the statement.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: Before, my piece ___.
I made this change: ___.
I chose it because ___.
After, I noticed ___. My next step is ___.
stages.say: Date the actual revision. Record the original state, one change made, the pupil's reason, the real after state and a next step. Keep the actual work or a precise witness comparison. Mark a new fold print as a revised version and retain the first version. Scribe exact words if useful, read them back and allow correction. State the true medium and support; no improvement is invented and no planned change is counted as made.
stages.good: A dated arts-log entry shows a real before-and-after revision in the same form, with a specific reason and honest evaluation. It records pupil choices separately from adult observation.
stages.fallback: Take an oral or gestured log after witnessing both actual silent versions. The adult retains precise action notes and the pupil's confirmed reason when recording is available.
stages.answer: Example only: Before, my sequence ended straight after the curve. I added a long pause. I chose it to help calm. After, I noticed the ending felt clearer to me. Next I will practise the same pause again.

Supported: Find the real before state and one wish.
Make or direct one small real change.
Show the changed part to an adult.
Keep both states and your own reason.
Independent: Make the one change from your wish.
Compare the same kind of work before and after.
Log the actual change, reason and effect.
Aspire: Complete the real revision and log.
Explain how it builds on one of your stars.
Use a detail from before and after to support your view.
Set one next step from the real result.

log: Before, my real piece or sequence ___.
I made this change: ___.
I chose it because ___.
After, I noticed ___.
The before and after records are ___.
My next step is ___.
misconceptions: Writing a wish means the work has improved
A planned sentence is not a made change. Carry out one small action and keep the real before and after states or precise witness notes.
An old dry print must be physically altered
A new version on fresh paper can be the revision. Retain the original, label the new version and compare the two actual prints.
Every change must be called better
Record the observed effect honestly. If a change does not help, select and try a smaller achievable action. Do not invent a successful result.
A new medium can be compared as if it were the same piece
Compare like forms. If access requires a new medium, create a fresh dated baseline in that form and then make a real revision to it.
kit: For four pupils: four actual chosen pieces or accurate witnessed sequences, four two-stars-and-one-wish reviews and tests, four books or arts logs and four pencils. Have four labelled spaces to retain both real states.
Provide the four picture-and-word prompts, or display and read them aloud. Prepare one actual adult before version and a real same-form revision for the demonstration.

Use only the resources needed for each agreed wish. Visual routes may need eight small spare sheets and familiar drawing tools. Paint uses a small amount of familiar washable non-toxic paint, five brushes, four mats, two stable water pots, cloths and flat drying space.

Fold-print revisions use fresh paper and the safe four-step method. Keep dry originals intact. Prepare four new sheets plus four spares if needed; use three small dabs, clear borders and gentle pressure.

Sound or silent revision needs a quiet seated space and a clear stop cue. A pupil may direct an adult. A recording device is optional; precise witnessed before-and-after action notes are enough. Keep sound below talking volume.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show the actual adult before state and chosen wish. Say: I keep this real starting point before I change one part.
15 to 30 seconds
Actually make one revised mark, fresh-print version or changed silent sequence. Say: I make my wish into an action, not just a sentence.
30 to 45 seconds
Place the two actual same-form states together, or perform both witnessed versions. Say: This is the one feature that changed.
45 to 60 seconds
Give a reason and honest effect. Say: I keep both states and name what really happened. A new fold print is labelled as a revised version.
models: Teacher model only: I kept the original silent sequence. I made its final pause longer. I chose that action to help calm. The after version has a pause I can notice more clearly.

Teacher model only: I kept my dry first fold print. I made a revised print on fresh paper with wider spacing. I kept both real prints and described the actual difference. I did not paint over or hide the first version.
lessons.cover: Find the actual chosen piece, review and one wish. If any are missing, make a tiny honest fresh piece and review it today. Keep a real before state, then help the pupil carry out one small wish in the same form. A dry fold print can have a new labelled version on fresh paper using the safe fold-print method; retain the first print. For no materials, actually perform or direct a silent baseline and revised sequence with one changed feature. Compare the real states, ask for the pupil's reason and record the observed effect. Do not count a planned sentence as an improvement. Retain before and after work or precise witness notes, with the true date, medium and support. Follow the seven-stage timing and final two Review minutes for tidy-up.

lessons.title: Review and choose one change
lessons.goal: I can review my real work and test one change for a reason.
success: I can review my intention, features and real progress.
I can choose one small change and test it.
I can record the actual result and my next step.
words: review
Look or listen again and say what you notice.
intention
What you want your work to suggest.
feature
A part you can notice in the work.
feedback
A comment about the work that may help a choice.
revise
Make a change for a reason.
effect
What a feature seems to do.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real plan, piece and process record.
Use a quiet or private route if helpful.
stages.say: Recover the real plan and work or precise live-sequence record. We review what actually exists. If the plan or piece is missing, agree a small honest plan and make a simple new starting piece or sequence now, dated today. It becomes today's starting point, not invented earlier work.
stages.good: The pupil identifies their actual work, intention and starting condition. A new catch-up record is labelled with today's date and source. No old image or decision is fabricated.
stages.fallback: Read back the real sequence note or let the pupil direct a short current sequence. If no record exists, witness a small new starting sequence today.
stages.answer: A real new starting point is valid. It cannot be labelled as evidence of an earlier stage.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Review your intention and one feature.
Name the form or tools, what is made and the help used.
stages.say: Use five short review prompts. What did you want the work to suggest about resilience? Which feature helps that idea? What form or materials did you use? What is actually made so far? What help did you use? You can say that a part is unfinished.
stages.good: The pupil gives or confirms a structured self-review grounded in the plan and actual piece. Staff distinguish intended meaning from observed features and note support honestly.
stages.fallback: Ask one prompt at a time through speech, sign or gesture. Adult reads a precise current-state note back for pupil confirmation.
stages.answer: A specific feature might be a turn, repeated mark, pause or original phrase. The maker explains the intention; a neatness judgement is not the review.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch an adult review a real example.
See one small change being tested.
A test can help, stay similar or need another try.
stages.say: My plan says the path should show finding another route. I notice the turn is hard to see. I used dry marks, and the small piece is made. My one test is to make the turn clearer on a small test area. I compare it with the real starting feature and say what changed. I do not claim better unless I can explain the effect. For a quiet sequence I could test one pause. These are adult models.
stages.good: The adult uses intention, feature, form/materials, progress and help, then tests one achievable revision. The real starting point and actual effect are distinct. Pupils see that feedback and a test support a choice rather than force praise.
stages.fallback: Perform or direct two quiet or silent versions differing in one feature. Adult describes the actual change and effect. A device or art materials are not needed.
stages.answer: Check: Should the maker change everything at once? No. A small change makes its effect easier to judge. If unclear, compare changing one pause with changing the whole sequence.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Use self-review or ask for one comment.
A private peer comment needs both people to agree.
Choose one change for your own intention.
You or the peer may stop. Self or staff review is enough.
stages.say: First review the work yourself. A staff comment can help. If you want one private peer comment, choose one part to show and ask the peer too. Either person can stop. The peer says one feature they notice and its possible effect, with no marks or rankings. Hinge: which route is valid? A force a peer to comment, B use self-review or a staff comment if peer feedback is not used, or C invent a peer comment. Explain. Use at most one peer comment across both periods; retain this actual comment for the second lesson if used.
stages.good: The pupil chooses B and retains ownership of the change. If peer feedback is used, both agree, only one chosen part is shown privately and one feature-based comment is retained. If not used, the actual route is labelled without penalty.
stages.fallback: Use oral self-review or a private staff comment on the actual observed sequence. Record peer comment not used, declined, unavailable or stopped, as true.
stages.answer: If A or C is chosen, state that feedback is optional and must be real. Parallel check: If either person says stop, do we stop and use staff or self-review? Yes. Continue when the pupil recognises a valid alternative.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Choose one small change from your review.
Test it in your actual form or a small test version.
Keep the real starting feature and the test result.
Record what the test did and what you will revise next time.
stages.say: Choose one change that could help your intention and can be done with available tools and access. Test only that feature. Keep the real current-state note and actual test, then say whether the effect helped, stayed similar or needs another try. You may direct an adult. Keep the same form when possible. If access requires a new form, make a new dated starting point in that form before the test.
stages.good: One achievable revision is tested and retained with a reason and actual effect. The structured review leads to a clear next making step. No improvement is assumed and an access change alone is not presented as artistic progress.
stages.fallback: Perform or direct a planned quiet or silent sequence, then revise one pause, order detail or action. Adult witnesses both actual versions and retains precise notes and the pupil's reason.
stages.answer: A test may make a turn clearer, lengthen a pause or change one original phrase. The pupil's actual form and intention determine the change. A real unsuccessful test remains useful evidence.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Compare the real feature and test.
What did the change do? What will you try next?
Keep the comment route and your decision honest.
stages.say: Use one feature as evidence for your view. Say what changed, what helped or did not help, and the small revision you intend to make in the second period. Record self, staff or one private peer comment as the route actually used. A peer route can be declined or stopped. Use the final two minutes to tidy and store the actual work, test and log.
stages.good: The pupil links a real test to the intention and chooses a manageable next revision. The feedback route is accurate and no person judgement or public display is introduced.
stages.fallback: Adult reads both observed versions and the pupil's decision back. A private oral review is enough. Retain a precise note rather than inventing media.
stages.answer: Useful: The longer pause made the restart clearer to me. Or: The wider turn did not help, so I will try a shorter line. Both are honest test reviews.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: I notice ___.
My test changed ___. The effect was ___.
My next revision is ___ because ___.
stages.say: Date the real review and test. Record the intention, chosen feature, one test, actual effect, help and next revision. Add the feedback route and state clearly if a peer comment was not used, declined, unavailable or stopped. I can scribe your words and read them back.
stages.good: The dated arts log links actual work, a specific change test and a next revision. It accurately separates the pupil's view from any staff or optional peer comment.
stages.fallback: Pupil gives an oral or gestured log. Adult retains precise actual observations and exact confirmed words at the next recording opportunity.
stages.answer: Example only: I notice the restart is unclear. I tested a longer pause. It felt clearer to me. I used a staff comment, not a peer comment. Next I will use the pause in my piece.

Supported: Review one prompt at a time with an adult.
Choose one small change. Test it.
Tell or show what the test did.
Keep the real record and next revision. Peer feedback is optional.
Independent: Review intention, features, form, progress and help.
Choose and test one small change.
Record the real effect and one next revision.
Use self, staff or one agreed private peer comment.
Aspire: Use your real review and test.
Explain why the change fits your intention.
Say what a comment helped you notice, or use self-review.
The next level task is optional.

log: My intention and a feature I notice are ___.
My form, progress and help were ___.
I tested ___ because ___.
The actual effect was ___.
Feedback route: self / staff / one agreed private peer comment.
Peer comment: used / not used / declined / unavailable / stopped.
My next revision is ___.
misconceptions: A comment tells the maker what they must do.
The maker considers a feature-based comment and chooses a change for their intention. Feedback is advice, not an instruction to please someone.
Everyone must show work to a peer.
Peer feedback is optional. Both people agree, one chosen part is shown privately, and either can stop. A staff comment or self-review completes the core task.
A revision must make the result better immediately.
Make a purposeful change and record its actual effect. An unsuccessful test is retained honestly with a next step. Do not claim improvement without evidence.
A missing old image or comment can be made up later.
Use the real current work and notes. Make a new dated starting point if needed. State when a peer comment was not used, declined or unavailable.
kit: For five pupils: five actual selected plans, five actual pieces or precise live-sequence records, five arts logs and five pencils. Keep the Week 4 process evidence with each pupil's own work.

Prepare only resources needed for the small chosen revisions. A dry visual route might use five small test spaces and ten colour tools shared in pairs. Retain before and after notes without covering the original record.

If the actual medium needs paint: six familiar brushes, five mats, three stable water pots, small amounts of familiar non-toxic paint and cloths. Keep wet work flat and away from electrical items. No new tool is compulsory.
If the piece uses paper parts: up to ten prepared scraps and three glue sticks for small tests. Use torn or prepared parts if cutting is a barrier, following local procedures.
For original sound, words or silent movement: a quiet seated space, the actual sequence or text note, and a start and stop cue. No recording device, instrument or copied text is required.
Optional private peer route: one short feedback prompt per pair, with an adult checking consent on both sides. A peer, public share or recorded media is not required for the lesson.
Adult model: one original piece or sequence, its short plan, a real starting-state note and one actual feature revision. All samples remain labelled teacher models.
demo: 0 to 15 seconds
Show the actual adult plan and piece. Say: I wanted a new route. I notice the turn is hard to see.
15 to 30 seconds
Name the actual form, state and help. Say: I choose one small turn change, not a whole new design.
30 to 45 seconds
Make a real small test and compare it. Say: This is what changed. I will describe the actual effect.
45 to 60 seconds
Record the next revision and true feedback route. Say: I used self-review. No peer comment was used. This is an adult model.

stretch.label: Optional next level stretch
stretch.task: Use your review to explain one strength and one need. Link your test to the intended effect. Say how a real comment or your own review shaped the choice. Plan one next revision.
stretch.evidence: Keep the real work reference, structured review, actual test, feedback route, your reasons and next revision.
stretch.why_optional: This task is extra. Your Explore work is complete without it. Keep the record in case your next level changes.
stretch.good: The pupil weighs actual evidence against intention, explains a feedback or self-review decision and proposes a specific feasible revision. Peer feedback is not required.
stretch.fallback: Adult witnesses the real versions and records the same review in exact confirmed pupil words, clearly naming the actual feedback route.

models: Teacher model only: My plan meant to show another route. I notice the turn is hard to see. I tested a shorter line. The turn looked clearer to me. I used self-review and no peer comment. Next I will revise that line in the piece.
Teacher model only: My quiet sequence has a restart. I tested a longer pause, but it felt too slow to me. I will try a smaller pause change next. I keep the actual test, even though it did not help.
lessons.cover: Recover the real plan, actual work and process note. If missing, make a small dated plan and current starting piece or sequence. Use the five self-review prompts, model one achievable feature change and let pupils test it. Self-review or a staff comment is enough; optional private peer feedback needs both people's consent and stops on request. Keep the real test and next revision for period two. Follow the seven-stage timing.

staff_guidance.plain_language: A review notices what the real work does and chooses one manageable change. Resilience can include a pause, help, practice or a new method. Do not treat an unsuccessful trial as personal failure or insist on a positive result.
staff_guidance.scope: Both lessons are Explore review-and-revision lessons. Structured self-review and one actual purposeful revision form the core. Peer feedback is optional, and a staff comment or self-review is sufficient. Optional next level tasks add reasoned evaluation without changing the core requirement. No award completion or public event is inferred.
staff_guidance.art_specialist_help: Read the pupil's real plan and look at the actual work or witnessed sequence. Ask what it was meant to suggest, which feature does that, what materials or form were used, what is complete and what support was needed. Help the pupil choose one small achievable change. Model a real before state, change one feature and describe the actual result. Judge intention, action and a reasoned view rather than polished adult technique.
staff_guidance.sensory_and_emotional_access: Use the existing invented or abstract idea. No personal hardship or public performance is required. Offer quiet or silent seated work and a private audience. Keep sound below talking volume and stop on a raised hand. A pause or request for help is valid. Either person can refuse or stop optional peer feedback.
staff_guidance.safety: Check the actual planned revision against familiar available tools, space and access. Keep wet materials on mats and store work flat. Use prepared or torn paper if needed. Ask before touching work. A pupil may direct adult handling. Keep the same medium for a fair comparison when possible. If access requires a different form, record a new dated starting point in that form before revising it.
prompt_ladder: Point to the place or instruction.
Model the first step only, then return the task.

adaptations.cognition_and_learning: Use the same short review questions: intention, feature, form/materials, progress and help. Choose one change rather than many. Model one action and fade the prompt.
adaptations.communication_and_interaction: Accept speech, sign, gesture, a sketch or an adult scribe. Give processing time. Use I notice ... I will change ... because ... . Read exact scribed words back for correction.
adaptations.semh: Keep the maker in control of feedback and audience. Peer comments require both people's agreement and may stop at any point. Staff or self-review is enough. Discuss the work, never the person.
adaptations.sensory_and_physical: Offer silent seated actions, large marks, familiar tools or pupil-directed adult handling. Record actual help and any change of access. Do not treat an access switch alone as proof that the artwork improved.
adaptations.eal: Review and explain in any language. Model notice, change and effect with an original short example. Accept a labelled sketch or short oral account before fuller sentences.

staff_guidance.careers_line: Artists and designers review a brief, consider feedback, revise a feature and explain what the change did.
staff_guidance.peer_consent: Peer feedback is optional. Ask the maker if they want one comment on one chosen part, then ask the peer if they want to give it. Proceed only when both agree. Show that part privately to one peer; this is not a public display. Either person can withdraw before or during the exchange. The peer gives one comment about a feature and its possible effect, with no marks, ranking or judgement of the person. The maker decides what to use. If declined, withdrawn or unavailable, use a staff comment or self-review and label the actual route. Do not invent a peer comment. At most one peer comment is used across the two periods. If one was given in lesson one, reuse that real comment rather than ask for a second. If none has been used, the optional route may be offered in lesson two with fresh agreement from both people.

cold_call.middle: What one small change could help your intention?
cold_call.higher: What does the actual test show, and how did your review shape the choice?

ta_focus.I do: Point to the real starting feature and actual test. Do not supply a pupil opinion or claim a better result.
ta_focus.We do: Check consent on both sides before optional private peer feedback. Offer self or staff review without penalty.
ta_focus.Independent: Keep the actual change test, support and next revision. Label the feedback route honestly and scribe exact words.

lessons.evidence: Retain the actual plan and work or honest new dated starting point, structured self-review, chosen feature, real small revision test, actual effect, support and next revision. Record the true feedback route. If no peer comment is used, say so rather than fabricating one.
lessons.artist_use_note: This week reviews and revises original pupil work. All adult models remain separate. No reproduced artwork, lyrics or artist quotation is supplied.

hinge.question: Peer feedback is not used. Which route still completes the core task?

options.B: Use self-review or a staff comment

hinge.feedback: B is a valid route. Keep the real review, test and your own decision.
hinge.wrong_feedback: Peer feedback is optional and must be real. Which route uses an honest alternative?

peer_feedback.default: Off. Self-review or a staff comment is a complete route.
peer_feedback.consent: Both the maker and the peer agree before one chosen part is shown privately.
peer_feedback.limit: At most one private peer comment across the two periods. Reuse a real earlier comment instead of asking for another.
peer_feedback.withdraw: Either person may stop. Close the chosen work and use self or staff review.
peer_feedback.comment: One feature and its possible effect. No marks, rankings or judgement of the person.

lessons.title: One real revision and its effect
lessons.goal: I can make one chosen change and record what it actually did.
success: I can use my real review and choose one revision.
I can make that change and keep a true before and after record.

words: review
Look or listen again and say what you notice.
intention
What you want your work to suggest.
feature
A part you can notice in the work.
feedback
A comment about the work that may help a choice.
revise
Make a change for a reason.

What a feature seems to do.

stages.name: Arrival
pupil: Find your real piece, review and test.
Name the one change you chose.
stages.say: Recover the real plan, current work, review and test from Monday. State the one feature you intend to revise. If records are missing, use a new small dated starting point and an honest self-review now. Do not invent an earlier piece, comment, test or photo.
stages.good: The pupil identifies an actual starting state and a chosen manageable revision. Missing earlier evidence remains visible and any catch-up work is dated today.
stages.fallback: Read back the actual live-sequence note. Pupil confirms it or directs a new short starting sequence if needed.
stages.answer: Use what really exists. A new current starting point supports today's revision without proving an earlier history.

stages.name: Starter
pupil: Show what the work is meant to suggest.
How could your one change help that idea?
stages.say: Look at the intention from the real plan or today's honest catch-up plan. Which feature will change? How could the change affect the resilience idea? Keep the aim small enough to do today. A change of access may be needed, but it is not proof of artistic improvement.
stages.good: The pupil names one achievable revision and a possible intended effect. They keep the same medium where possible or establish a fresh baseline if access requires another form.
stages.fallback: Pupil states, signs or directs the intended change to a quiet or silent sequence. Adult records the real starting actions before the revision.
stages.answer: A clear aim might be make one turn easier to see, shorten a pause or replace one original word. The reason should relate to the maker's intention.

stages.name: I do
pupil: Watch one real change being made.
Compare the actual before and after feature.
The result may help or need another try.
stages.say: Here is my actual starting feature. I shorten this line to make the turn easier to see. That is a real revision, not just a promise to change. I compare the before note and the actual new line. I explain whether the effect helped. If it did not help, I retain the true test and choose another next step. For a silent piece I change one pause and perform both actual versions. These are adult models.
stages.good: The adult makes one concrete revision and compares a real before state with its actual result. No better outcome is assumed. A reversed unsuccessful trial remains labelled as a real attempted change, not hidden.
stages.fallback: Perform or direct two actual quiet or silent versions with one revised feature. Adult notes the precise before and after actions, effect and decision.
stages.answer: Check: Which shows revision? A saying I might change later, B changing one actual feature and recording its effect, or C copying an adult's finished example. B. If unclear, model the difference between planning and doing one change.

stages.name: We do
pupil: Use one real review comment or self-review.
Direct one change in a class example.
Say what actually changed.
One private peer comment is optional. Both agree and either may stop.
stages.say: Use the class example's intention and one real feature observation to direct a small change. This is still adult model work, not your evidence. Optional peer feedback follows the same consent rule: both agree, one chosen part, one private comment and either may stop. Hinge: a real revision did not help the intended effect. Should we A pretend it improved, B hide the test, or C keep the true test and plan a next step? Explain. If a peer comment was already given on Monday, use that actual comment and do not ask for a second. Only if none has been used may the one optional comment be offered today.
stages.good: The pupil chooses C and describes the actual attempted change without inventing success. Self or staff review remains enough. Any optional peer comment is consensual, private and feature-based.
stages.fallback: Pupil directs an adult to change a quiet or silent example. Use self-review or a staff observation, then read the actual effect back for confirmation.
stages.answer: If A or B is chosen, model an honest unsuccessful trial. Parallel check: If a longer pause feels less clear, can the maker record that and try a smaller change next? Yes. Continue when a truthful result and next step are accepted.

stages.name: Create
pupil: Make your one chosen revision in the real piece or sequence.
Keep the actual before and after feature.
Say what changed and what effect you notice.
Record help and a truthful next step.
stages.say: Make the chosen change now in the actual piece or sequence. Retain a genuine before note or observed starting version and the real revised result. You may direct adult handling. Compare the changed feature with your intention and explain the effect. If the test is unhelpful, keep its record and choose a next step; you may restore a previous feature for a reason, but the actual attempted revision remains visible. Do not treat a different medium alone as an improvement.
stages.good: One real purposeful revision is made and logged. The before and after states are actual, support is recorded and the pupil gives a reasoned account of the effect. The work can remain unfinished. A planned or merely retained feature alone does not replace the revision action.
stages.fallback: Perform or direct the planned quiet or silent sequence, change one action, order detail, pause or original phrase, and perform or direct the revised version. Adult witnesses both actual versions and scribes the pupil's view and support.
stages.answer: A revision can help, stay similar or reveal another need. The action and real effect are kept even when a later version restores the earlier feature. Never recreate an old photo and label it as earlier evidence.

stages.name: Review
pupil: Show the actual changed feature and both real records.
Did the change help your intention? Say why.
Keep the real result, support and next step.
stages.say: Describe the chosen revision and a feature that supports your view. Say what helped or did not help. Keep the actual current version and truthful state, finished or still being made. Record self, staff or the one agreed private peer comment as actually used; state if peer feedback was declined, unavailable, stopped or not used. Use the final two minutes to tidy and store the work and records together.
stages.good: The pupil evaluates an actual revision against intention, records support and gives a manageable next step without automatic praise or completion claims. Optional feedback remains private and accurately labelled.
stages.fallback: Adult reads the real before and after sequence notes back. Pupil confirms, corrects or adds their own view. Private oral review is sufficient.
stages.answer: Useful: I shortened the pause. The restart felt clearer to me. Or: The new line did not help, so I kept its test record and will try a different gap next.

stages.name: Exit
pupil: Arts log: Before I ___. I changed ___. After I ___.
The effect was ___ because ___.
My next step is ___.
stages.say: Date the real revision. Keep the starting feature, change, actual result, effect, support and next step together. Note the actual feedback route, including when no peer comment was used. I can scribe your exact words and read them back. Today's Explore revision work is complete without the optional next level task.
stages.good: The log demonstrates one actual purposeful revision and an honest evaluation. It does not claim guaranteed improvement, a completed award or a public share.
stages.fallback: Pupil confirms an oral or gestured review of the real versions. Adult retains precise observations and exact pupil words when recording materials are available.
stages.answer: Example only: Before, the pause was long. I made it shorter. After, the restart felt clearer to me. I used self-review and no peer comment. Next I will check the ending.

Keep actual before and after records.
Explain the effect, support and next step.
Use self or staff review if a peer comment is not used.

Explain how the change affects your intention.
Evaluate a real comment or your self-review.
The next level task is optional.

Label the actual feedback route, including peer comment not used, declined, unavailable or stopped. An unsuccessful test remains visible.
lessons.artist_use_note: This week reviews and revises original pupil work. All adult models remain separate. No reproduced artwork, lyrics or artist quotation is supplied.

hinge.question: A real revision did not help the intended effect. What should the maker do?

options.C: Keep the true test and plan a next step

hinge.feedback: C keeps the actual revision and its effect honest. Choose a useful next step.
hinge.wrong_feedback: An unsuccessful trial is still real evidence. Which option records it truthfully and supports another step?

review_steps: Find the real review and choose one revision.
Look at the real before and after effect.
Log the result, support, feedback route and next step.
review_fields: The materials or form I used ___.
What is made and the help I used ___.
Feedback route: self / staff / one private peer comment ___.
Peer comment used / not used / declined / unavailable / stopped ___.
The real result and next step ___.
lessons.peer_consent: Peer feedback is optional. Ask the maker if they want one comment on one chosen part, then ask the peer if they want to give it. Proceed only when both agree. Show that part privately to one peer; this is not a public display. Either person can withdraw before or during the exchange. The peer gives one comment about a feature and its possible effect, with no marks, ranking or judgement of the person. The maker decides what to use. If declined, withdrawn or unavailable, use a staff comment or self-review and label the actual route. Do not invent a peer comment. At most one peer comment is used across the two periods. If one was given in lesson one, reuse that real comment rather than ask for a second. If none has been used, the optional route may be offered in lesson two with fresh agreement from both people.
process_steps: Find the real review and choose one revision.
Look at the real before and after effect.
Log the result, support, feedback route and next step.

peer_feedback.default: Off. Self-review or a staff comment is a complete route.
peer_feedback.consent: Both the maker and the peer agree before one chosen part is shown privately.
peer_feedback.limit: At most one private peer comment across the two periods. Reuse a real earlier comment instead of asking for another.
peer_feedback.withdraw: Either person may stop. Close the chosen work and use self or staff review.
peer_feedback.comment: One feature and its possible effect. No marks, rankings or judgement of the person.
peer_feedback.honest_log: Record used, not used, declined, unavailable or stopped as true. Never invent a comment.

improvement_record: The effect I notice and why ___.

scope: Both pathways work at Explore. Each lesson is complete without the optional GROW next level stretch. Week 5 contributes evidence towards the ongoing arts log and does not by itself complete an award. This is classroom arts learning. No live arts encounter or future event is claimed.
timing: Arrival 0-3; Starter 3-6; I do 6-12; We do 12-18; Create 18-32; Review 32-37; Exit 37-40 minutes. Tidy in the final two minutes of Review.
